candidates.designation: b (Tuomi et al. 2019, Table of planet candidates, row GJ406 b)
candidates.tier_reason: Single-survey long-period RV signal (K = 9.6 +/- 5.0 m/s, 99% interval) from HARPS+HIRES, never independently recovered. Bowens-Rubin et al. 2023 added HIRES, MAROON-X and CARMENES velocities, found nothing above 0.1% FAP after removing the 2.7 d rotation signal, and their RadVel fits of b did not converge. They explicitly neither refute nor confirm it; imaging rules out >4 M_Jup (age < 1 Gyr).

considered_not_added.name: Wolf 359 c
considered_not_added.reason: refuted: the 2.687 d RV signal (Tuomi et al. 2019) matches the stellar rotation (2.705 d); refuted by Lafarga et al. 2021 (CARMENES activity indicators, arXiv:2105.13467), as tabulated in Bowens-Rubin et al. 2023 Table 'Exoplanet Candidates Identified by Tuomi 2019' ('false positive'). exoplanet.eu still lists it as Confirmed; OEC as Controversial.

considered_not_added.name: AD Leo b
considered_not_added.reason: refuted: the 2.23 d RV signal (Tuomi et al. 2018; Tuomi 2019 table row GJ388 b, P=2.22599 d, Msini 23.1 Me) is the stellar rotation. Carleo et al. 2020 (GAPS XXI, arXiv:2002.10562) is titled '...refutation of AD Leo b'; Kossakowski et al. 2022 (arXiv:2209.05814) and Carmona et al. 2023 (arXiv:2303.16712, 'no evidence for a corotating planet') agree. exoplanet.eu lists it Controversial. AD Leo has no other planet claim in either catalogue, so no new system is proposed.

considered_not_added.name: LP 427-16 b
considered_not_added.reason: not a planet claim: Baroch et al. 2021 (A&A 653, A49) find an SB1 long-term RV trend and bound the companion to 0.011-0.13 Msun (P 6,400-29,000 d); a low-mass star or brown dwarf. exoplanet.eu lists it as a 12 M_Jup candidate from the lower bound only.

considered_not_added.name: HIP 36985 b (GJ 282 C b)
considered_not_added.reason: brown dwarf / stellar: Grandjean et al. 2020 Msini 29 M_Jup (exoplanet.eu page); Baroch et al. 2021 fit RVs + NACO astrometry and derive dynamical masses for the GJ 282 C pair (P = 6591 d, i = 94 deg). Not a planet.

considered_not_added.name: HD 38858 b
considered_not_added.reason: refuted/retracted: the 407 d, 30.6 M_E signal (Mayor et al. 2011) was declared spurious by the discovery team's follow-up, an alias of the 2930 d magnetic cycle (Kennedy et al. 2015, Sect. 2); Flores et al. 2018 (A&A 620, A34) tie the RV variation to the 10.8 yr cycle.

considered_not_added.name: HD 85512 b
considered_not_added.reason: refuted: Laliotis et al. 2023 (1,127 additional RVs) do not detect the 58.43 d signal of Pepe et al. 2011; a 51.2 d signal takes over, matching predicted rotation and S-index periods; they 'assert that the reported companion HD 85512 b ... is not caused by a physical planet' (Sect. HD 85512; table class ACT-R*). exoplanet.eu: Controversial.

considered_not_added.name: HD 26965 b (omi2 Eri A b, 40 Eri Ab)
considered_not_added.reason: refuted as activity: the 42.3 d signal (Ma et al. 2018) sits on the rotation (39-43 d); Rosenthal et al. 2021 call it a false positive from rotation and Laliotis et al. 2023 classify it ACT* ('reported as a planet ... but we believe it to be stellar'). Burrows et al. 2024 reach the same conclusion (recalled, not verified this session). exoplanet.eu: Retracted.

considered_not_added.name: bet Vir b
considered_not_added.reason: not a planet claim: Endl et al. 2016 (ApJ 818, 34) report the ~2040 d RV variation of HD 102870 as 'probably caused by stellar activity, rather than reflexive Keplerian motion' (abstract). exoplanet.eu nonetheless lists it as Candidate.

considered_not_added.name: HD 150248 b
considered_not_added.reason: stellar companion: Jenkins et al. 2015 (spectroscopic binaries from AAPS) give K = 1995 m/s at P = 3272 d; exoplanet.eu's 0.1 'M_Jup' is almost certainly 0.1 M_sun (its own remark flags the ambiguity). Not a planet.

considered_not_added.name: HD 145825 b
considered_not_added.reason: stellar: dos Santos et al. 2017 (MNRAS 472, 3425) find a 0.10 Msun red dwarf on an 18 yr orbit (Msini 106 M_Jup). exoplanet.eu: Retracted.

considered_not_added.name: HD 145825 c
considered_not_added.reason: not a planet claim: dos Santos et al. 2017 note that residuals of 17 AATPS points peak near 725 d and an extra 0.70 M_Jup, e=0.87 object improves the fit, but HARPS residuals do not show it and they 'need more observations to securely infer ... if it truly has an extra substellar companion'. A residual-fitting exercise on 17 points, not called a candidate. Writer may override (would be 'unlikely').

considered_not_added.name: HD 184860 b
considered_not_added.reason: brown dwarf: Msini 32 M_Jup (Vogt et al. 2002, 'Ten Low-Mass Companions from the Keck Precision Velocity Survey', per exoplanet.eu page); host is a K2+K7 binary (SIMBAD).

considered_not_added.name: HD 68017 Ab
considered_not_added.reason: brown dwarf: Msini 34.9 (+7.6/-7.3) M_Jup, P ~40000 d (Hirsch et al. 2021 via exoplanet.eu; RV+imaging). exoplanet.eu: Controversial.

considered_not_added.name: zet Her Ab
considered_not_added.reason: no planetary claim: Morel et al. 2001 infer a third body of <50 M_Jup in the zeta Her binary, 'compatible either with a brown dwarf or a giant planet' (exoplanet.eu remark); no orbit. Not added.

considered_not_added.name: eta Cas Ab
considered_not_added.reason: retracted/refuted: Kane et al. 2025 (AJ 170, 270), 'No Giant Planets in the Eta Cassiopeiae System' (exoplanet.eu: Retracted).

considered_not_added.name: HD 104304 b

considered_not_added.name: HD 112758 Ab

considered_not_added.name: BD+20 1790 b
considered_not_added.reason: refuted: Carleo et al. 2018 (A&A 613, A50) 'Multi-band high resolution spectroscopy rules out the hot Jupiter BD+20 1790b'. Also beyond scope check: Gaia parallax 36.09 mas (SIMBAD), inside 100 ly, so the refutation is the reason.

Web search found no other source. Reported plainly as untraceable; not added.
